shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tall vertical stone surface
bilateral symmetry about a central vertical axis
circular ring / disc motif set on the central axis
paired crescent or arc-shaped curved elements
paired motifs flanking the axis in the upper zone
horizontal banded division of the surface into registers
fan or radiating line pattern (rayed head in A, incised lines on the upper block in B)
justification: Both are tall, narrow, vertically stacked relief surfaces organised symmetrically about a central axis, with paired curled/looped motifs in the upper zone, a single ring or disc on the axis in the middle, and broad crescent-like arcs sweeping across the lower register — that specific sequence is the strongest correspondence. The decisive difference is that A is a legible, cleanly outlined anthropomorphic figure (head, arms, hands, legs) rendered in crisp, evenly modelled relief with dotted detailing, whereas B's motifs are abstract, shallow and weathered on a coarse rounded monolith with no figure discernible.
